 :JUDGMENT:
The Petitioner has filed the Petition against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 17.03.2019 at about 5.00 p.m. the Petitioner was boarded the Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-06-D-5040 at Bengaluru and was sitting back left tyre seat, the same was driven by its driver on NH-150(A) Road in a rash and negligent manner without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding at about 8.45 p.m., near Revanna Miltry Hotel, Chikkanayakanahalli Town, Tumkur District, due to his negligence driving the left back tyre burst, due to which, the left upper iron plotform broken, consequent to which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

entities.text: Regional Office No.301, 2 B, Unity  Building-11A Cross, P. Kalling  Rao Road, Mission Road  Bengaluru-560027
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
Immediately after the accident, Petitioner was shifted to Chikkanayakanahalli Govt. Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter was referred to Kadur Govt. Hospital, wherein he was referred to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein, he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Loader at Wooden godown under S.M. Associates and was earning Rs.17,928/- per month.

3. The Petitioner has contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bus bearing Reg.No. KA-06-D-5040 which is owned by the Respondent No.1 and insured with Respondent No.2.
As such, the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
4. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed detailed Objection Statement.
Despite of service of notice, the respondents No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
5. Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner.
It has admitted the issuance of policy to Bus bearing No.KA-06-D-5040.

Further it contended that owner of the insured Bus has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c)
Shekrappa vs K.G. Shivaprasad on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195820104/
2 and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
The driver of bus had no valid driving licence to drive the bus and entrusted the vehicle to a person who had no valid driving licence.
Hence, there was breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending bus by its driver.

Further it contended that the petitioner sustained injuries because of tyre burst and it is the duty of the insured keep the vehicle in road worthy conditions to safe guard the passengers and as well as public.
Because of tyre burst the flat from opened and because of that petitioner had sustained injuries and not because of rash and negligent act of driver.
It is further contended that at the time of accident, the Bus was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of Bus.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 17.03.2019 at about 8.45 p.m. on NH-150(A) road, near Revanna Miltry Hotel,
Chikkanayakanhalli Town, Tumkur District, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-06-D-5040?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents at Ex.P1 to 19.
He further got examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.P.20 to 22.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any evidence.
8. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

9. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 :

As per the Final Order,

Issue No.1:-
It is the case of the Petitioner that he has sustained injuries in the accident caused by the driver of the offending Bus bearing No.KA-06-D-5040.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
11. In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked in total 22 documents.

12. Upon going through the said documents, it shows that on the complaint lodged by one Ravi R.,
Chikkanayakanahalli police have registered FIR against the driver of the offending bus bearing No.KA-06-D-5040 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P18 Spot panchanama, shows that the concerned police have drawn the same in the presence of panchas.

Ex.P.2 is the charge sheet, it discloses the fact that after thorough investigation, the IO has charge sheeted the driver of offending bus in question for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 and 5 are the Wound Certificates, they show that petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
13. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Shekar M., as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P.20 to 22 i.e., Entire case sheet, Disability calculation sheets and X-rays.
PW.3 who is the Orthopaedic surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Jayanagara, Bengaluru re-iterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Jayanagara
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.

15. Though the Respondent No.2 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Though the respondent No.2 taken contention that accident taken place due to tyre burst and not because of rash and negligent act of driver.
This contention is not acceptable one.
Because as per the contents of the FIR and charge sheet, the driver of the Bus driven the same in rash and negligent manner by which the back left side tyre burst and accident has occurred.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.

16. Issue No. 2 - As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 36 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.8 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 04.07.1983.
The accident took place on 17.03.2019.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is 36 years which is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
18. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was working as a Loader at a godown under SM Associates and was earning Rs.17,928/- per month.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.11 Pay slip for the month of January 2021 to February 2020, 2019, to prove his income.
Wherein, his net salary was shown as Rs.17,921/-p.m.
But to prove the said avocation and his income he has not examined his employer.
Admittedly, it is a private establishment.
Hence, in the absence of the evidence of his employer, the said salary certificate could not be considerable.
Therefore, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has occurred in the year 2019, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.14,000/- p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
20.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-3 and 5 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling tenderness left foot and heel 2. Swelling tenderness right foot and heel wherein, the Doctor has opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.2 has also re-iterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident.

21. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
22.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
23.

The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 18.03.2019 and discharged on 17.04.2019 at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma &
Orthopedics.

sentences.text: Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 31 days.
25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, atleast it took two months for recovery.
I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,000/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
26.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
27. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.1,20,000/- towards medical expenses.
He has produced 24 medical bills at Ex.P.15 amounting to Rs.13,041/-.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills totally amounting to Rs.13,041/, which is rounded up at Rs.13,000/

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.13,000/ as a compensation under this head.
VI
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
28. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is unable to carry out his day to day activities.
29. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. Shekar as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Entire case sheet, Disability calculation sheets and X-rays at Ex.P.20 to 22.
He assessed permanent disability of both lower limbs to the whole body of 21.09%.
30. In the cross-examination, PW.2 has admitted that after discharge from the hospital, he has assessed the disability of petitioner.
He has admitted that fracture is mal united.
He admitted that implants are removed.
Further he admitted that he is not required external support.
He has also admitted that he has personally operated and treated the petitioner.
31. The Doctor has assessed permanent disability of both lower limbs to the whole body of 21.09%.

Upon careful consideration of the assessment of disability made by PW.2 keeping in mind the fact Shekrappa vs K.G. Shivaprasad on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195820104/
6 that PW.1 personally appeared before this court and deposed, also keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 and the treatment which he has taken

entities.text:
Shekrappa vs K.G. Shivaprasad on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195820104/
6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed appears to be at the higher rate.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 20% would be just and proper.
32. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of Rs.14,000/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 20%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.5,04,000 /- (Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 15 x 20/100 =Rs.5,04,000/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,04,000/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
33.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 20,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 13,000/-
5. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 28,000/-
up period 6 Loss of Future earnings Rs.5,04,000/-

Total Rs.6,03,000/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,03,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
34. Regarding Liability : As already discussed above, in this case the driver of the offending bus bearing No.KA-06-D- 5040 was charge-sheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 2 as "Partly in the Affirmative".
35. Issue No.3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.6,03,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
